subject: Computer Networking
title: HTTP/2 and HTTP/3
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on HTTP/2 and HTTP/3.

hook.text: HTTP/1.1 loads one thing at a time per connection. HTTP/2 loads many in parallel on one connection.

buildup.text: HTTP/2 uses multiplexing: multiple streams share one TCP connection. No more head-of-line blocking at HTTP level.

discovery.text: Header compression with HPACK shrinks repetitive headers. Server push preloads resources before the browser asks.

twist.text: TCP still has head-of-line blocking. One lost packet stalls all streams. HTTP/3 fixes this with QUIC over UDP.

climax.text: HTTP/3 uses QUIC: encrypted by default, faster handshakes, and independent streams. Packet loss affects only one.

punchline.text: HTTP/2 multiplexes. HTTP/3 eliminates TCP's limits. Faster web, less waiting.

quiz.question: What transport protocol does HTTP/3 use instead of TCP?

details.summary: HTTP/2 introduced multiplexing, header compression, and binary framing to speed up the web. HTTP/3 replaces TCP with QUIC over UDP, eliminating head-of-line blocking and reducing connection setup latency.
details.whyItMatters: HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 fundamentally changed web performance. Understanding them explains why modern sites load faster and helps developers optimize for these protocols.
takeaways: HTTP/2 multiplexes multiple requests over a single TCP connection
HTTP/3 uses QUIC over UDP to eliminate TCP head-of-line blocking
Both are backward-compatible and negotiated automatically

faq.question: Do developers need to change code for HTTP/2 or HTTP/3?
faq.answer: No code changes are required. Browsers and servers negotiate the protocol version automatically. However, some HTTP/1.1 optimization techniques like domain sharding and sprite sheets become unnecessary or counterproductive.

faq.question: Why does HTTP/3 use UDP instead of TCP?
faq.answer: TCP's head-of-line blocking means one lost packet stalls all streams on the connection. QUIC over UDP handles each stream independently, so packet loss affects only the impacted stream. QUIC also combines the TLS handshake with connection setup, saving a round trip.
